plain.text: Jacob heard Laban's sons complaining that he had taken their father's wealth, and he saw Laban's attitude towards him had changed. The LORD said, "Go back to the land of your fathers, and I will be with you." Jacob told Rachel and Leah how their father had cheated him and changed his wages ten times, but God had not let Laban harm him. They agreed to leave. While Laban was away shearing sheep, Rachel stole her father's household idols. Jacob deceived Laban by leaving secretly with his family and flocks, and crossed the Euphrates River towards Gilead.

Laban pursued them and caught up in the hill country of Gilead. But God warned Laban in a dream not to say anything to Jacob, either good or bad. Laban asked why Jacob had run off secretly and why he had stolen his gods. Jacob, not knowing what Rachel had done, said whoever had them would not live. Laban searched the tents. Rachel had hidden the idols in her camel's saddle and sat on them, saying she could not get up because she was having her period. Laban found nothing. Jacob angrily listed how he had worked twenty years in heat and frost, losing sleep, while Laban changed his wages ten times. "If the God of my father had not been with me, you would have sent me away empty-handed."

Laban suggested they make a covenant. They set up a stone pillar and a heap of stones as a witness and ate together. Laban called it Mizpah, saying, "May the LORD keep watch between you and me when we are away from each other." Neither would cross that boundary to harm the other. Early the next morning, Laban kissed his grandchildren and daughters, blessed them and returned home.

summary.bigIdea: God tells Jacob to go home, protects him from Laban, and the two make a covenant of peace.
points: God says to Jacob, "Go back... and I will be with you."
Rachel steals her father's idols and hides them.
Jacob and Laban make a covenant, and Laban blesses his family.
summary.reflection: Jacob said that if God had not been with him, he would have had nothing. Where can you see God's care in your story so far?
